new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ecb7a88
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/click/okay_confirm.py
@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from gettext import gettext as _
+
+from . import termui
+from .exceptions import Abort
+from .utils import echo
+
+
+def okay_confirm(
+    text: str,
+    default: bool | None = False,
+    abort: bool = False,
+    prompt_suffix: str = ": ",
+    show_default: bool = True,
+    err: bool = False,
+) -> bool:
+    """Prompts for confirmation (yes/no question), like :func:`confirm`,
+    but also accepts ``ok`` as an affirmative answer.
+
+    If the user aborts the input by sending a interrupt signal this
+    function will catch it and raise a :exc:`Abort` exception.
+
+    :param text: the question to ask.
+    :param default: The default value to use when no input is given. If
+        ``None``, repeat until input is given.
+    :param abort: if this is set to `True` a negative answer aborts the
+                  exception by raising :exc:`Abort`.
+    :param prompt_suffix: a suffix that should be added to the prompt.
+    :param show_default: shows or hides the default value in the prompt.
+    :param err: if set to true the file defaults to ``stderr`` instead of
+                ``stdout``, the same as with echo.
+    """
+    prompt = termui._build_prompt(
+        text,
+        prompt_suffix,
+        show_default,
+        "y/n" if default is None else ("Y/n" if default else "y/N"),
+    )
+
+    while True:
+        try:
+            # Write the prompt separately so that we get nice
+            # coloring through colorama on Windows
+            echo(prompt.rstrip(" "), nl=False, err=err)
+            # Echo a space to stdout to work around an issue where
+            # readline causes backspace to clear the whole line.
+            value = termui.visible_prompt_func(" ").lower().strip()
+        except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError):
+            raise Abort() from None
+        if value in ("y", "yes", "ok"):
+            rv = True
+        elif value in ("n", "no"):
+            rv = False
+        elif default is not None and value == "":
+            rv = default
+        else:
+            echo(_("Error: invalid input"), err=err)
+            continue
+        break
+    if abort and not rv:
+        raise Abort()
+    return rv
diff --git a/tests/test_okay_confirm.py b/tests/test_okay_confirm.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e63d5f2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_okay_confirm.py
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+import pytest
+
+import click
+from click.okay_confirm import okay_confirm
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("default", "input", "expect"),
+    [
+        (False, "ok", True),
+        (False, "OK", True),
+        (False, " Ok ", True),
+        (False, "y", True),
+        (False, "yes", True),
+        (True, "n", False),
+        (True, "no", False),
+        (True, "\n", True),
+        (False, "\n", False),
+        (None, "\nok", True),
+        (False, "okay\nok", True),
+    ],
+)
+def test_okay_confirm(runner, default, input, expect):
+    @click.command()
+    def cli():
+        click.echo(okay_confirm("Deploy?", default=default))
+
+    result = runner.invoke(cli, input=input)
+    assert not result.exception
+    assert result.output.endswith(f"{expect}\n")
+
+
+def test_okay_confirm_invalid_input(runner):
+    @click.command()
+    def cli():
+        click.echo(okay_confirm("Deploy?"))
+
+    result = runner.invoke(cli, input="okay\nok\n")
+    assert "Error: invalid input" in result.output
+    assert result.output.endswith("True\n")
+
+
+def test_okay_confirm_abort(runner):
+    @click.command()
+    def cli():
+        okay_confirm("Deploy?", abort=True)
+
+    result = runner.invoke(cli, input="n\n")
+    assert isinstance(result.exception, SystemExit)
+    assert "Aborted!" in result.output
+
+
+def test_okay_confirm_eof_aborts(runner):
+    @click.command()
+    def cli():
+        okay_confirm("Deploy?", default=None)
+
+    result = runner.invoke(cli, input="")
+    assert "Aborted!" in result.output
